cards.explanation: The answer is sackcloth and sandals. The LORD tells Isaiah, "Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and the sandals from your feet." (Isaiah 20:2). Sackcloth was the cloth Isaiah wore around his waist. I wear an apron around mine, and I'd feel pretty exposed without it. And the verse says Isaiah did so, walking around naked and barefoot.

The answer is False. After the LORD's command, the text says, "And Isaiah did so, walking around naked and barefoot." (Isaiah 20:2). No argument and no asking for a different sign. Isaiah just does it. Friends, that is a hard thing to do, and he did it.

The answer is Egypt and Cush. The LORD says Isaiah went naked and barefoot "…as a sign and omen against Egypt and Cush…" (Isaiah 20:3). Cush is the land south of Egypt. Three years of walking around like that was a message for them, not just a strange habit.

The answer is that they'll be led away naked and barefoot. The LORD says the king of Assyria "…will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old alike, naked and barefoot…" (Isaiah 20:4). What Isaiah has been doing is what the captives will look like. The sign and the real thing match.

The answer is True. The LORD says the king of Assyria will lead away the captives and exiles, "…young and old alike…" (Isaiah 20:4). Both the young and the old are named right there in the verse. Nobody on that road is left out, friends.

The answer is shame. The LORD says the king of Assyria will lead them away "…to Egypt’s shame." (Isaiah 20:4). That's the word the text uses for what this brings Egypt. It's a small word, friends, but it carries the whole verse.

The answer is those who hoped in Egypt and Cush. The LORD says, "Those who made Cush their hope and Egypt their boast will be dismayed and ashamed." (Isaiah 20:5). They had put their hope in those two lands. Verse 4 speaks of Egypt's shame, and this verse adds the people who counted on Egypt and Cush.

The answer is how can we escape now. The coastland dwellers say, "How then can we escape?" (Isaiah 20:6). They had fled to Egypt and Cush for help against the king of Assyria. Now their source of hope is the one being led away. I think they're feeling pretty stuck.
